value.rationale: Family-size/leaf-count dependence is a natural whole-versus-part question. Exact finite parameter regressions show that larger rooted families have more internal leaves yet fewer global leaves on average; this resolves their opposite covariance signs, yields strict negative association with every nonconstant increasing size score, and identifies the unique degenerate boundary cases. The structural attachment-edge correction explains the effect.
